logic.note: Conducts A → C above its knee, blocks the other way.

timing.note: Switches instantly with each re-solve; no reverse-recovery (a Schottky has almost none).

analog.note: Piecewise linear: 0.25 V knee + 0.2 Ω, which gives about 0.27 V at 100 mA and 0.45 V at 1 A (datasheet typical 0.32 / 0.45 V at 25 °C). No exponential curve, no temperature drift.

power.note: Warns above 1 A average and above 20 V reverse; the part does not fail. Reverse leakage (up to ~1 mA hot) is not modelled.

emulates: Forward drop in a power path
Reverse blocking (stops USB back-feeding a battery)
doesNotEmulate: Exponential I-V curve below the knee
Reverse leakage, which grows a lot with temperature
testOnRealDevice: Measure the drop at your real load (VBUS vs the cell)
That the stripe faces the board: reversed, the device never powers on from the battery
